Python script to fetch June 2023 revisions and parse references:

import requests
import re
import mwparserfromhell

SESSION = requests.Session()
API = "https://en.wikipedia.org/w/api.php"

PAGES = [f"August {i}" for i in range(1, 32)]

status_re = re.compile(r"https?://(?:twitter|x)\.com/[^/]+/status/\d+", re.I)
archive_re = re.compile(r"https?://(?:web\.archive\.org|archive\.today|archive\.is)/[^"]+", re.I)

# Fetch the last revision before 2023-07-01

def fetch_june_rev(page):
    params = {
        "action": "query",
        "format": "json",
        "prop": "revisions",
        "titles": page,
        "rvlimit": 1,
        "rvdir": "older",
        "rvstart": "2023-07-01T00:00:00Z",
        "rvprop": "ids|timestamp|content",
        "rvslots": "main"
    }
    r = SESSION.get(API, params=params)
    data = r.json()
    page_obj = next(iter(data["query"]["pages"].values()))
    rev = page_obj.get("revisions", [{}])[0]
    content = rev.get("slots", {}).get("main", {}).get("content", "")
    return content

# Extract references and detect tweet citations

def find_tweet_citations(wikitext):
    citations = []
    wikicode = mwparserfromhell.parse(wikitext)
    for node in wikicode.filter_tags(matches=lambda n: n.tag == "ref"):
        ref_text = str(node)
        urls = status_re.findall(ref_text)
        if urls:
            # Try to extract date from template fields
            templates = mwparserfromhell.parse(ref_text).filter_templates()
            date = None
            for t in templates:
                if t.has("date"):
                    date = str(t.get("date").value).strip()
                elif t.has("access-date"):
                    date = str(t.get("access-date").value).strip()
            citations.append({"url": urls[0], "date": date})
        else:
            # Check archived links that resolve to a tweet (best-effort by presence of '/status/')
            arch_urls = archive_re.findall(ref_text)
            for au in arch_urls:
                if "/status/" in au:
                    citations.append({"url": au, "date": None})
    return citations

# Filter for August dates (any year), when determinable

def is_august(date_str):
    if not date_str:
        return False
    ds = date_str.lower()
    return ("aug" in ds) or ("-08-" in ds)

result = {}
for p in PAGES:
    wikitext = fetch_june_rev(p)
    cits = find_tweet_citations(wikitext)
    aug_cits = [c for c in cits if is_august(c["date"])]
    result[p] = len(aug_cits)

print("Counts per day (June 2023 revisions):")
print(result)
print("Total:", sum(result.values()))

Python script to fetch current pages and count Twitter/X links in references (simple regex):

import requests
import re
import mwparserfromhell

API = "https://en.wikipedia.org/w/api.php"
PAGES = [f"August {i}" for i in range(1, 32)]
status_any = re.compile(r"https?://(?:twitter|x)\.com/", re.I)

def fetch_current(page):
    params = {
        "action": "query",
        "format": "json",
        "prop": "revisions",
        "titles": page,
        "rvslots": "main",
        "rvprop": "content",
        "rvlimit": 1
    }
    r = requests.get(API, params=params)
    data = r.json()
    page_obj = next(iter(data["query"]["pages"].values()))
    rev = page_obj.get("revisions", [{}])[0]
    content = rev.get("slots", {}).get("main", {}).get("content", "")
    return content

counts = {}
for p in PAGES:
    wt = fetch_current(p)
    code = mwparserfromhell.parse(wt)
    c = 0
    for node in code.filter_tags(matches=lambda n: n.tag == "ref"):
        if status_any.search(str(node)):
            c += 1
    counts[p] = c

print("Current page counts of Twitter/X links:")
print(counts)
print("Total:", sum(counts.values()))
